reasons.agent: Developer (Sonnet) builds by default to spare quota.
reasons.builder: A single-module change with tests written first suits Sonnet.
reasons.checker: QA checks it because it changes when the gate's inputs are produced for every project.
reasons.cron: Every five minutes, as other flows.
reasons.mode: One small task; a flow lands it through the normal gate.
reasons.stop: Stop when the one task is done.

design: In `refresh` (hub/hub/project_checks.py:1671), stop calling `supersede` for in-flight runs cut from another tip; a task with a run in flight is skipped as today (`is_running`). When a run ends `failed` and main has moved since it was cut, and the failure is not confirmed as the task's own (`own_failure`), the Hub requests a run on the current tip, as `refresh` would have, so a failure that belongs to the old main does not stand. `_stop_run_on_older_work` (a new completion replacing the task's work) is unchanged. The `superseded` state stays for that case and for existing rows. The project-checks capability's superseded requirement is reworded at fold, and its stale gate requirement (`checks-wait-less-fresh-the-gate-still-requires-a-current-result`, which says a pass on an older tip must not count) is restated to match FR-9.

checked: task_check_runs on the operator's Hub (mode=ro): 19 superseded runs 1-3 Nov, 14 on 3 Nov
limits: Whether ending runs early ever surfaced a merge conflict sooner was not measured; landing still reports conflicts
The saving is estimated from three days of records, to be re-measured after the build
The test names in each how_to_check are proposed coverage: none exists yet

problem:
On the operator's Hub, 19 pre-review runs (about 8 hours of hub-tests) were ended as superseded between 1 and 3 November 2026 because master moved while they ran; 14 of them on 3 November alone, with two specs building in parallel. Each was then started again from the beginning. The waste grows with the number of tasks in flight, since every landing moves main and ends every other task's running check.

The rule that ends them (project-checks, `checks-wait-less-fresh-results-afte-a-superseded-run-is-replaced`) gives as its reason: "Finishing it produces a result the gate will refuse as stale anyway." That stopped being true when approved-work-merges-in-batches (FR-9) made a pass of a task's work count on any main tip: `refresh` documents it (hub/hub/project_checks.py:1675-1678) and `test_a_green_on_an_older_tip_counts_and_is_not_run_again` (hub/tests/test_checks_refresh_when_main_moves.py:289) proves it. Landing is gated by the batch's own run on the exact merged tree, which is unchanged. So the run that is ended would, if it passed, have been accepted, and the run that replaces it repeats the same work.

requirements.rationale: A pass of the task's work counts on any main tip (approved-work-merges-in-batches FR-9), so the result is usable; ending it repeated the same work and cost about 8 hours of hub-tests in three days.
requirements.statement: A pre-review check run that is in progress when its project's main tip changes MUST run to completion and record its own outcome (passed, failed or error) against the main tip it was cut from; it MUST NOT be ended, recorded superseded, or replaced because of that change.

requirements.rationale: That run checks work that no longer exists; its result could never be used.
requirements.statement: A pre-review check run whose task's own work is replaced by a new completion MUST still be ended, recorded superseded, and replaced by a run on the new work.
A main tip change while a task's run is in progress MUST NOT start a second run for that task; the task has at most one run in progress at any time.

requirements.rationale: The failure may belong to the old main, which has since moved; before this change the run would have been replaced on the new tip, so this keeps that outcome for failures only.
requirements.statement: When a run cut from a main tip other than the current one ends failed, and its failure is not confirmed as the task's own, the Hub MUST start a run for the task on the current main tip without anyone requesting approval.
A run cut from an older tip that ends with a failure confirmed as the task's own MUST return the task to its author exactly as a failure on the current tip does, with no extra run started.

in_scope: Pre-review check runs (task_check_runs) when the project's main tip moves, by the Hub's own merge or by the watcher noticing an outside commit
What happens after a run cut from an older tip ends failed
Rewording the project-checks capability requirements this changes, at fold
non_goals: Landing batch checks: a batch whose base moved is still superseded and requeued, because landing must check the exact merged tree
Ending a run because the task's own work changed (a new completion): unchanged
The limit of two concurrent runs per Hub
Which result the approval gate accepts: a pass on any tip already counts (FR-9) and still does
Any AgentWeave-specific check configuration (later slices of the roadmap)

summary: A task's pre-review check run that is still running when the project's main tip moves runs to the end and its result counts, instead of being ended as superseded and started again on the new tip. A run whose task's own work changed is still ended. Product behaviour, for every project.
